title: Tailscale 1.52.0 fails to connect to the Tailscale service on Windows
body: After updating from Tailscale 1.51.0 to 1.52.0 on Windows 10, starting Tailscale normally or after a reboot shows “Failed to connect to Tailscale service.” The reported version is 1.52.0 (t3c2ff1e4a-gfccfad18e), and the bug report LogID is d7215ddcb08bb19ce0ab4ea8bcfa79f9bee1ba3764701c131f3cd9fc888038c9. I also have ZeroTier and Clash for Windows installed.

symptoms_visible: After updating from Tailscale 1.51.0 to 1.52.0, I get “Failed to connect to Tailscale service” when starting it normally or after rebooting Windows 10.
N0.label: N0 service connection failure reported

symptoms_visible: Task Manager says the Tailscale Service is running, but the client still cannot connect to it.
Restarting the service does not change the error; another affected installation also remained unable to connect after rebooting, reinstalling, and downgrading.
N1.label: N1 running service remains unreachable

symptoms_visible: Running tailscaled.exe directly reaches “wgengine.NewUserspaceEngine” and then exits with a nil-pointer panic whose stack includes windows.UTF16PtrToString, wintun.logMessage, and wintun.CreateAdapter.
N2.label: N2 startup panic captured

symptoms_visible: My affected system uses Simplified Chinese rather than Traditional Chinese.
The failure was also reproduced with an en-US system locale, while other installations on both older and newer Windows builds could run Tailscale 1.52.0.
N3.label: N3 locale and Windows-version hypotheses tested

symptoms_visible: I found a WireGuard-signed wintun.dll under System32 dated 2021-08-02; its size differs from the copy associated with Clash for Windows.
Two other affected users report that Tailscale started working after they renamed the System32 wintun.dll; I have not reported testing that change on my own machine.
N4.label: N4 conflicting DLL isolated and workaround confirmed by other users

symptoms_visible: Other affected users can connect again after moving the conflicting System32 wintun.dll out of the search path, but I have not confirmed the result on my own system.
N_terminal.label: terminal workaround established but reporter verification absent

question_patterns: In Task Manager or the Services console, is the Tailscale Service running?
What state does Windows report for the Tailscale service?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, it is running. Restarting it does not help. Another of us also tried rebooting, cleaning the install folder and reinstalling, and downgrading, but still could not connect.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No, the Tailscale Service is stopped, and starting it manually makes the client connect normally.
The service is shown as running under a different process ID after each restart, but the same connection error remains.

edges.comment: Messages c0-c2. The original reporter confirmed that Windows reports the service as running and that restarting it does not help. The reboot, reinstall, and downgrade results came from kegns, another affected user folded into the simulated user side.

question_patterns: Please run tailscaled.exe from cmd.exe and paste its complete output.
What does the service executable print when you launch it directly from a command prompt?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It starts logging, prints “wgengine.NewUserspaceEngine(tun "Tailscale") ...”, and then panics with “invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference.” The stack includes windows.UTF16PtrToString, wintun.logMessage, wintun.CreateAdapter, wireguard-go tun.CreateTUN, and tstun.New.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: tailscaled.exe stays running and prints no panic; it creates the adapter successfully and only fails later while contacting the control server.
The goroutine number and program counter differ, but the stack still runs through UTF16PtrToString, wintun.logMessage, and wintun.CreateAdapter.

edges.comment: Messages c6, c12-c17. The reporter pasted the full panic in c16, while atomshadows and participant4 supplied matching traces. These affected users are folded together only for the shared startup-crash chain; kegns's access-denied output is not substituted for the reporter's trace.

question_patterns: Which Windows display language and system locale are configured on the affected computer?
Can you compare your language and region settings with the test machine?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I am using zh-Hans, Simplified Chinese. The test screenshot appears to be zh-Hant, Traditional Chinese, so my language setting is different.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I am also using Traditional Chinese, matching the test machine, and the same panic occurs.

question_patterns: Can the failure be reproduced with another system locale or on another Windows installation?
Please compare the result across the available Windows language and OS-version combinations.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The administrative locale is Chinese (Simplified, China), code page 936. I also tested en-US on Windows 11 23H2 and it still did not work. A Chinese Windows 11 21H2 VM worked after installing 1.52.0, and another work PC on 23H2 also ran 1.52.0 normally.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The crash occurs on every Simplified Chinese installation and disappears immediately when the same machines use an en-US system locale.

edges.comment: Messages c17-c23. The reporter distinguished zh-Hans from the maintainer's zh-Hant test in c20. Avatasia supplied the administrative-locale and cross-VM tests, and participant3 reported a working 23H2 machine. Those affected-user observations are folded together and show that neither locale nor 23H2 alone tracks the crash.

question_patterns: Can you inspect the relevant Windows directories for other copies of the dependency shown in the stack and report their dates, signatures, and sizes?
Are there additional copies of the crashing library outside the application directory?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I found wintun.dll under System32, dated 2021-08-02. Its digital signature is related to WireGuard. It is 729192 bytes, while the Clash for Windows copy I compared it with is 427552 bytes.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: There is no wintun.dll anywhere in System32, and module inspection shows that tailscaled loads only the bundled copy from its own installation directory.
The System32 copy has the same old date and WireGuard signature but a slightly different file size.

question_patterns: Can you use a module or process trace to report which copy of the crashing dependency the service actually loads?
Please compare the loaded module with the copy shipped in the application directory.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: When I install the packaged Tailscale build, the loaded DLL is the older copy from System32 rather than the copy in the application directory. The old library exposes a different log callback shape; running my separately installed tailscaled with the application-directory copy works.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The process trace shows the bundled application-directory DLL is loaded, and it has the expected callback interface, but the same null-pointer panic still occurs.

edges.comment: Messages c23-c31. The original reporter supplied the System32 file's date, signature, and size in c30. L1nxy, another technically skilled affected participant, supplied the module-loading comparison and callback-interface observation. Avatasia and kegns then independently reported that renaming the System32 copy restored operation; that unprompted confirmation is recorded on N4.

solution.intent: Prevent tailscaled from loading the incompatible wintun.dll found in System32: preserve a backup and move or rename that conflicting copy with administrator privileges, then restart Tailscale or reinstall 1.52.0 if necessary and verify that the service remains reachable.
solution.concrete_example: After confirming the file is the conflicting WireGuard wintun.dll, rename C:\Windows\System32\wintun.dll to a backup name from an elevated shell, then restart the Tailscale service. If needed, reinstall Tailscale so its bundled dependency is present. Confirm that tailscaled no longer panics and that `tailscale status` can connect before declaring the issue resolved.
solution.inference_hint: The collected evidence supports the final diagnosis that DLL search-path handling caused tailscaled to bind to an older, incompatible System32 wintun.dll. Connecting that loaded module and its callback mismatch to the nil-pointer panic is the technical inference; the reporter's raw evidence consists of the stack trace and the file's location, date, signature, and size.

edges.comment: Messages c24-c32. Two other affected users confirmed the rename workaround in c25-c26, and the maintainer stated that the DLL search-path handling was under investigation in c32. The original reporter only confirmed finding the System32 file and never reported applying the workaround, so this terminal node records an established diagnosis and workaround without claiming reporter-side resolution.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: tailscaled loaded an older, incompatible wintun.dll from System32 instead of the compatible bundled copy, and the resulting interface mismatch led to the startup panic.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the direct tailscaled stack trace, the discovered System32 DLL, and the module/version comparison rather than inferred from Chinese locale or Windows version alone.

Must recommend safely moving, renaming, or otherwise removing the conflicting System32 wintun.dll from the search path, then restarting Tailscale or reinstalling if needed so the bundled compatible dependency is used.

Must not claim that restarting the service, rebooting, reinstalling, downgrading, or changing locale by itself is the fix; those directions did not explain or clear the failure in the collected reports.
Must ask the original reporter to verify that tailscaled no longer panics and that the client can connect to the local service before declaring the reporter's system resolved.
Must not state that the original reporter confirmed the workaround; only other affected users reported recovery after renaming the System32 DLL.

persona_hint.experience_level: Moderately technical Windows user who can inspect services, run executables from cmd.exe, paste a Go panic trace, and examine DLL metadata. More advanced module-loading analysis comes from another affected contributor folded into the user side.
persona_hint.communication_style: Brief and direct, with exact command output when requested. Cooperatively compares locale and file details and distinguishes observed facts from speculation.
